sections.title: Interface
sections.intro: KrystalField puts a wide real-time display on top and its two compressors side by side below it, around the controls that set the level window. Scroll to go through each part.

steps.title: User Interface
steps.text: The display fills the top half, with the preset bar along its bottom edge. Below it, the DOWN-WARD and UP-WARD sections sit on either side of the controls for the level window and the timing, between the input and output meters. Input gain and mix are on the left, makeup and Automatic Loudness Matching on the right, while the detector, the clipper, oversampling and the GR, LU and GI readouts run along the top.

steps.title: Detector, Clipper and Oversampling
steps.text: MODE chooses how KrystalField reads the level: RMS for a smooth response, PEAK to catch every transient, LOUD to follow the loudness you actually hear. CLIP keeps the output below 0 dB, with a soft or a hard clipper, and OS runs the processing at up to 8 times the sample rate for a cleaner result with fast settings.

steps.title: Target and Range
steps.text: TARGET sets the level you want the track to sit around, RANGE how far it may move around it. Together they draw a window: the loud parts above it are turned down, the quiet parts below it are brought up, and everything inside passes untouched. Click the link between the knobs to set the upper and lower threshold separately instead.

steps.title: Downward Compression
steps.text: The DOWN-WARD section turns down everything above the window. RATIO sets how firmly it holds the loud parts, up to a limiter-like 100:1 as in the Maximizer preset here, and KNEE how gradually it starts, from Hard to Soft.

steps.title: Upward Compression
steps.text: The UP-WARD section brings up everything below the window: quiet details, room sound and tails come forward without touching the loud parts. RATIO sets how much they are lifted, and KNEE how gradually, and also how much the very quiet parts, such as noise, are left alone.

steps.title: Attack and Release
steps.text: Both sections share a single gain change, so one attack and one release time them both. ATTACK sets how quickly the gain comes down, when a loud part arrives; RELEASE how quickly it comes back up, when the loud part ends or a quiet part needs lifting.

steps.title: Real-Time Display
steps.text: The display shows the last 6 seconds of signal against the two thresholds, drawn as dashed lines with the target between them. The gain reduction of the downward section hangs from the top in purple, the gain increase of the upward section rises from the bottom in green, and the loudness runs across with its value in LU.

steps.title: Presets
steps.text: Eight factory presets cover mastering, drums, vocals and parallel processing, and you can save your own. Open the list to search it, step through the presets with the arrows, and save or delete your own from the same bar.

steps.title: Input, Mix and Lookahead
steps.text: The INPUT knob sets the level going into the processing. The MIX slider blends the original back in for parallel processing, at 60% here, and the LOOKAHEAD slider lets KrystalField see up to 20 ms ahead, so it catches transients cleanly even with a fast attack.

steps.title: Makeup, Loudness Matching and LF Bias
steps.text: MAKEUP sets the level coming out. AUTO turns on Automatic Loudness Matching, which keeps the output as loud as the input so you judge every setting by its sound, and shows the gain it applies below the button. LF BIAS keeps the low end from driving the processing, so kick and bass don’t pump a full mix.

steps.title: GR, LU and GI Readouts
steps.text: The readouts along the top show at a glance how hard each section is working: GR for the gain reduction of the downward section, GI for the gain increase of the upward section, and LU for the short-term loudness of the output. They turn orange and then red when the processing or the loudness gets heavy, as the 9.1 dB of gain increase here.

steps.title: Input and Output Meters
steps.text: The input and output meters show the level going in and coming out, with RMS and peak level for each channel, and the readouts below hold the highest peak until you click them. The power button in the top bar bypasses the plugin, perfectly in time.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Pay what you want on itch.io, or enter 0 to get the full version for free. Free for personal and commercial use.

steps.title: Install
steps.text: Run the installer, or copy the plugin files yourself: VST3 on Windows, AU and VST3 on macOS.

steps.title: Read the Manual
steps.text: Every control in detail, with tips, ranges and defaults.

install.title: Install
install.intro: KrystalField is available on itch.io as pay what you want: enter 0 to download the full version for free. The download contains both the installer and the plugin files, so you can choose how to install it.

manual.title: Manual
manual.intro: KrystalField is a dynamics processor that turns the loud parts down and brings the quiet parts up at the same time, keeping a track inside the level range you choose. This manual covers every control, with tips, ranges and defaults.

chapters.title: Getting Around
intro: Start here if you are new to KrystalField. The Quick Start gets you to a good result in a few steps, and the topics that follow explain how the signal moves through the plugin and how to find your way around the plugin window.

topics.title: Quick Start
body: If you just want to start shaping your dynamics, this is the fastest way to a good result:

steps: Pick a preset from the bar at the bottom of the display, or start from Default Settings.

Set TARGET to the level you want the track to sit around, and RANGE to how far it may move around it. The two dashed lines in the display show where the loud parts start being turned down and the quiet parts start being brought up.
Use the RATIO knobs of the DOWN-WARD and UP-WARD sections to decide how firmly each side holds the level.
Turn on AUTO for Automatic Loudness Matching, and set CLIP to SOFT or HARD to keep the output below 0 dB.

body: Use the MIX slider to blend some of the original back in, and watch the GR, GI and LU readouts at the top to see how much the plugin is working.

topics.title: Signal Path
body: Processing always follows the same order:

steps: The detector listens to the input, after the input gain, with the low end reduced by LF bias.

From the same level, the downward section works out how much to turn down the parts above the upper threshold, and the upward section how much to bring up the parts below the lower threshold. The two are combined into a single gain change, smoothed by the attack and release.

The audio is delayed by the lookahead, so the gain change can start before the signal it reacts to, and the input gain is applied. The input meters read the signal at this point, and the dry signal for the mix is taken here.
The gain change, the makeup gain and the gain from Automatic Loudness Matching are applied, followed by the clipper, at a higher sample rate with oversampling on.
The dry/wet mix blends the result with the dry signal. The output meters and the loudness readout read the final signal.

body.note: The same gain change is applied to both channels, so the stereo image never shifts.

head: Area
What it holds
rows: Detector, clipper and oversampling selectors (MODE, CLIP, OS), the GR, LU and GI readouts, the bypass button and the Krystal Dynamics logo for information and updates
Real-time display with the threshold lines, the legend, the zoom button and the display settings (gear)
The preset bar: Save, previous, preset list, next, Delete

topics.title: Adjusting Controls
body: Drag knobs and sliders up and down, or use the mouse wheel. Knobs show their value below: click it to type a new one. The MIX, LOOKAHEAD and LF BIAS sliders fill up with their value, which is shown next to them.
MODE, CLIP and OS change with each click, moving to the next value. AUTO, bypass and the link button switch on and off.

more.title: What You Can Automate
body: Every control that affects the sound can be automated from your DAW (see Parameter Reference). TARGET and RANGE write two parameters together, the upper threshold and the range, so their automation follows exactly what you do on the knobs. The display zoom, the link button and the settings belong to the user interface and can’t be automated.

topics.title: Help Bar
body: The bar along the bottom of the plugin window gives a short description of whatever control you are hovering over. Otherwise it reads Hover any control for details.

topics.title: Resizing the Plugin Window
body: Drag the lower-right corner to resize the plugin window, in 5% steps from 50% to 115% of the original 1000 × 750. A popup shows the current scale while you drag, and the size is saved with the session.

topics.title: Latency
body: With lookahead and oversampling off, KrystalField adds no latency. Lookahead adds a fixed 20 ms whatever its value, and oversampling adds the latency of its filters. The total is reported to your DAW and compensated automatically, so KrystalField stays sample-aligned with the rest of your tracks.

chapters.title: Dynamics
intro: KrystalField keeps a track inside a window of levels. Above the upper threshold it works as a downward compressor, turning the loud parts down; below the lower threshold it works as an upward compressor, bringing the quiet parts up. Between the two, the signal passes untouched.

topics.title: Target and Range
body: TARGET sets the level you want the track to sit around, and RANGE how far it may move around it. The upper threshold, where downward compression starts, sits half the range above the target; the lower threshold, where upward compression starts, half the range below. With the defaults, the window goes from −24 to −12 dB.

figure.caption: TARGET and RANGE with the link button between them, and the timing controls below.

body: Click the link button between the two knobs to set the thresholds separately instead: the knobs become UPPER and LOWER, and each moves its own threshold. The thresholds always stay at least 3 dB apart. Both are drawn as dashed lines in the display, with the target between them while the knobs are linked.

body.note: A narrow range holds the level tightly, for a dense, even sound; a wide range lets more of the natural dynamics through.

topics.title: Downward Compression
body: The DOWN-WARD section turns down whatever goes above the upper threshold. RATIO sets how firmly: at 4:1, a signal 8 dB over the threshold comes out only 2 dB over it, and from 20:1 up the section behaves like a limiter. KNEE decides how gradually it starts around the threshold, and reads Hard, Medium or Soft.

topics.title: Upward Compression
body: The UP-WARD section brings up whatever falls below the lower threshold. RATIO sets how firmly: at 2:1, a signal 10 dB under the threshold comes out only 5 dB under it. Quiet details, room sound and tails come forward, while the loud parts are left to the downward section.

KNEE decides how gradually it starts around the lower threshold, and also how the noise floor is treated. With a hard knee everything below the threshold is brought up, however quiet; the softer the knee, the more the very quiet parts, such as noise and silence, are left where they are.

topics.title: Attack and Release
body: Both sections share one gain change, so the attack and release work for both. ATTACK sets how quickly the gain comes down, when a loud part needs turning down or the boost of a quiet part needs taking away. RELEASE sets how quickly it comes back up, when a loud part ends or a quiet part needs bringing up.
A fast attack catches transients, a slower one lets them through for punch. A short release makes the processing more audible and energetic, a long one smoother and more transparent.

topics.title: Lookahead
body: The LOOKAHEAD slider lets KrystalField react before the signal arrives: the audio is delayed, so the gain change can start up to 20 ms ahead of a peak, and is held for the same time so it lasts through it. Transients are caught cleanly even with a fast attack.
Any value above 0 ms adds a fixed 20 ms latency, compensated by your DAW.

topics.title: Detector
body: The MODE button chooses how KrystalField reads the level:

head: Mode
Character
rows: Follows the average level over a short window: a smoother, more musical response
Follows the peaks instantly: a sharper, faster response that catches every transient
Follows the perceived loudness, weighted like the human ear, the same way LUFS is measured: the processing follows how loud the music sounds rather than its peaks

topics.title: LF Bias
body: The LF BIAS slider reduces the low end in the signal the detector listens to, with a high-pass filter. Raise it so kick and bass stop driving the processing of a full mix; at 20 Hz the detector hears the full range. The sound of the track itself is not filtered.

topics.title: Oversampling
body: Fast gain changes and clipping create harmonics, and at normal sample rates some of them fold back into the audible range as aliasing. The OS button applies the gain change and the clipper at 2, 4 or 8 times the session sample rate, so the result stays clean with fast settings and with the clipper on. Higher factors use more CPU and add some latency, compensated automatically.

chapters.title: Gain, Mix and Clipper
intro: Input gain drives the signal into the processing, makeup gain sets the level coming out. The dry/wet mix blends the original back in, Automatic Loudness Matching keeps the output matched to the input, and the clipper keeps it below 0 dB.

topics.title: Input Gain
body: Set with the INPUT knob. With the thresholds fixed, more input gain pushes more of the signal above the upper threshold and less of it below the lower one. The dry signal used by the mix includes the input gain.

topics.title: Makeup Gain
body: Set with the MAKEUP knob and applied after the processing, before the clipper and the dry/wet mix.

topics.title: Dry/Wet Mix
body: Set with the MIX slider, it blends the processed signal with the original, kept in time with it. Values below 100% give parallel processing: the density of heavy compression with the natural dynamics of the original.

topics.title: Automatic Loudness Matching
body: Processing changes the loudness, and a louder signal tends to win a comparison even when it doesn’t sound better. Automatic Loudness Matching measures the loudness of the input and of the output and compensates the difference, so you can judge each setting at the same level. Turn it on with the AUTO button; the gain it applies is shown below it.

more.title: When the Loudness Is Measured
body: Loudness is measured with K-weighting, the same weighting used for LUFS, over a window of about 3 seconds. After you change a parameter that affects loudness, the measurement starts again once the window has been refreshed. Changes to makeup gain, dry/wet mix, the clipper, oversampling and bypass don’t restart it.
The applied gain is saved with the session.

topics.title: Clipper
body: The CLIP button keeps the processed signal below 0 dB after the makeup gain:

head: Mode
What it does
rows: No clipping: the output can go above 0 dB
Rounds the peaks off smoothly as they approach 0 dB, with a touch of saturation

body.note: The clipper works on the processed signal before the dry/wet mix: with MIX below 100%, the dry signal is not clipped.

chapters.title: Presets
intro: Presets store every setting of KrystalField, so you can start from a sound that already works and save your own.

topics.title: Factory Presets
body: The preset bar at the bottom of the display opens the list of presets. Click the name to open it, type in the search box to filter it, and use the arrows on either side to step through the presets one by one. Factory presets and your own are listed in separate groups.

head: Factory preset
rows: The starting point, with every control at its default
A limiter-like downward section with the full 20 ms of lookahead and a gentle lift of the quiet parts, for maximum loudness
Low ratios on both sides and the LOUD detector, for transparent control of a full mix
Moderate downward and gentle upward compression with the RMS detector, for a denser, more even sound
Firm downward compression over a wide range, for a loud, dense master
Heavy processing on both sides blended with 40% of the original
A narrow 8 dB window and the LOUD detector, to keep a vocal at a steady level
Punchy downward compression with LF bias at 80 Hz, so the kick doesn’t drive the whole bus

topics.title: Saving Your Own
body: Click Save, give the preset a name, and it joins the list under your own presets; saving with the name of an existing preset asks before overwriting it. Delete removes the selected preset of your own; factory presets can’t be deleted.
Your presets are stored in Documents/Krystal Dynamics/KrystalField/Presets, one file per preset, so you can back them up or move them to another computer.

chapters.title: Monitoring
intro: The readouts at the top show how hard each section is working and how loud the output is, and the meters show the level on both sides of the processing.

topics.title: GR, LU and GI Readouts
body: The readouts in the top bar show, from left to right, the gain reduction of the downward section (GR), the short-term loudness of the output (LU) and the gain increase of the upward section (GI). GR and GI hold their highest value for a moment before falling back, and turn orange above 6 dB and red above 9 dB. LU turns orange above −14 LUFS and red above −11 LUFS.

The input meters, labelled IN, show the level after the input gain; the output meters, labelled OUT, show the final output. Each has a bar for the left and the right channel: the bar shows the RMS level, with the peak level drawn on top.
The readouts below hold the highest peak of either channel until you click them to reset. Output peaks above 0 dB are shown in red.

topics.title: Bypass
body: The power button in the top bar bypasses all processing so you hear the original signal. It keeps the same latency, so switching never shifts the timing, and the change is ramped to avoid clicks. While bypassed, the meters, the readouts, the display and the AUTO value stay frozen until you switch back.

chapters.title: Real-Time Display
intro: The real-time display shows the last 6 seconds of signal against the two thresholds, with the gain reduction from the top and the gain increase from the bottom, so you can see exactly what both sections are doing.

topics.title: Display Traces

figure.caption: The display with the Drum Bus Enhancer preset.

head: Trace
What it shows
rows: The level of the signal after the input gain
How much the downward section turns the signal down, drawn from the top
The short-term loudness of the output, with its value in LU
How much the upward section brings the signal up, drawn from the bottom
The level of the final output

body: The upper and lower thresholds are drawn as dashed lines, with the target between them while TARGET and RANGE are linked. Click an entry in the legend to hide or show its trace.

topics.title: Zoom
body: The button at the lower right of the display sets how far down the scale goes, and changes with each click.

after.note: The display zoom is saved as a preference and with the session.

chapters.title: Settings and Updates
intro: Choose light or dark themes and set how much CPU the user interface uses. The Krystal Dynamics logo gives you the version, updates and credits.

topics.title: Display Settings
body: The gear in the lower-left corner of the display opens the settings.

Set the knobs, the background and the display to light or dark independently. If you are short on CPU, a lower frame rate and Low graphics, which leaves out the shadows, lighten the load of the user interface. The sound is not affected.

topics.title: What Is Saved Where
body: Preferences apply to every instance and are stored in Documents/Krystal Dynamics/KrystalField/preferences.xml.

topics.title: Updates and Information
body: Click the Krystal Dynamics logo in the top-right corner for the version, credits and links. KrystalField checks the website for new versions: when one is out, the logo lets you know and the plugin window shows what’s new, with a download link. The check only reads the latest version number and sends no personal data.

chapters.title: Parameter Reference
intro: All automatable parameters, in the order they appear in your DAW.

history.title: Version History
history.intro: Everything new in each release. KrystalField checks for updates on its own and lets you know in the plugin window when a new version is out.
